caption_L1: Utilities industry energy inputs in the U.S. from 1997 to 2018 (in billion U.S. dollars) is a area plot. Year is plotted with a linear scale of range 2000 to 2015 along the x-axis. The y-axis shows Energy inputs in billion U.S. dollars with a linear scale with a minimum of 0 and a maximum of 150.
caption_L2L3: The graph opens in 1997 with an energy input of 60 billion dollars. The input increased to around 110 billion dollars by the year 2000. The input continued to increase to the year 2005 when it reached its peak of 140 billion dollars. For the five years from 2005 to 2010, the input markedly decreased to around 90 billion dollars. However, there was a sharp rise from 2010 to 2014, when the input reached approximately $130 billion. This was followed by the sharpest decline, plummeting to around $65 billion by 2016. The input has since recovered, with growth through to 2018, returning to $90bn.
